title: [WT-18] Docs: worktree mode in the narrative guides and the worker role docs
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §0, §2, §3, §6 and §7.6.

Objective: agents and humans reading the guides learn the worktree delivery path, and the worker role doc stops telling workers never to use .worktrees/. This is the other half of the docs sweep, split from WT-17 for the 5-file cap.

Deliverable:
- Root CLAUDE.md, 'Working in this repo' and Landing: the worktree mode summary (per-task W on moe/task/<id>, landing to main by merge-tree + CAS, board history on refs/moe/board, control checkout on moe/control) and the settings key list.
- scripts/CLAUDE.md, 'Land on every exit': a worktree-mode arm covering L0-L14, the unlanded route, DENY in W, the control-seat no-op, removal and sweep. Keep the shared-mode text intact.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, 'Delivery Path': the worktree variant; the daemon stays state-only.
- docs/roles/worker.md line 13 ('work in the project root ... never a .worktrees/ checkout') becomes mode-aware: in worktree mode the wrapper has already put you in your task worktree. Keep the role doc within the 40-line lint cap.
- docs/roles/worker.reference.md: the using-git-worktrees row and the attribution paragraph gain the worktree-mode behaviour.
- A VS Code note (no code change) goes in CLAUDE.md's package table row.
Read the landed code for spellings.

NOT in scope: MCP_SERVER, SCHEMA and CONFIGURATION (WT-17); TROUBLESHOOTING (WT-16); code; .moe/roles copies (the plugins sync them).

Verification: npm run lint && grep -q 'moe/task/' CLAUDE.md && grep -q 'worktree' scripts/CLAUDE.md && grep -qi 'worktree' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md && grep -qi 'worktree mode' docs/roles/worker.md
definitionOfDone: Root CLAUDE.md describes worktree mode (moe/task/<id>, landing to main, refs/moe/board, moe/control, settings.worktreeMode) and mentions the VS Code no-change note.
scripts/CLAUDE.md 'Land on every exit' has a worktree-mode arm naming the L-steps' codes and the unlanded route, with the shared-mode text unchanged.
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Delivery Path describes the worktree variant and keeps 'the daemon is state-only'.
docs/roles/worker.md and worker.reference.md are mode-aware about .worktrees/, and npm run lint (40-line cap) passes.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/CLAUDE.md: a worktree-mode arm in a NEW bullet directly after the existing `- **Land on every exit**` bullet. That bullet must stay byte-identical (DoD 2): never edit it, and give the new bullet a different bold name, e.g. `- **Land on every exit, worktree mode**`.

FIRST, build a spelling inventory from the LANDED code (keep it outside the repo).
- Grep scripts/moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 for every helper, code, env var and ref the design names: sync_land_target, reconcile_push, take_unlanded_route, denied_wt, task_branch_landed, board_snapshot, follow_control_checkout, their ps1 twins, the MOE_WORKTREE_* / MOE_LAND_* / MOE_CONTROL_* / MOE_BOARD_* / MOE_PUSH_* codes, --land-branch/-LandBranch, MOE_WORKTREE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SEC, MOE_LAND_LEASE_WAIT_SEC.
- Grep the daemon for resolveWorktreeMode, workspaceMode, landingRetry and the 'unlanded' outcome.
- Where code and docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md disagree, the code wins. List each mismatch in the completion summary for WT-19.

Cover, from §1-§4, §6 and §7.2, with sub-bullets as needed:
- Scope. The mode is pinned per attempt from the claim / get_context `workspace` (absent = shared). Only a worker on a WORKING claim gets W = <top>/.worktrees/<taskId> on moe/task/<taskId>: locked, sparse '/*' '!/.moe/', reused across sessions. The pre-flight guards report_blocked with their codes, launch no CLI and never fall back to the shared checkout. CLIs run in W while MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control checkout.
- Attribution in W. No baseline, no tiers: every non-DENY dirty path is the task's. DENY in W has no BOARD exception and adds .claude/skills/**. MOE_WORKTREE_STRAY_EDIT is reported, never landed or reverted.
- Checkpoints: L0-L2 onto the task branch (checkpointPush, never forced).
- Completion L0-L14, one clause per step with its code:
  - the lease only while a qualityGate is set;
  - remote mode: B = refs/remotes/origin/<target>, the non-forced push is the only publication and the local target is a mirror;
  - every completion journals before publishing and is gated while a qualityGate is set (scope ignored), in a .moe-free sparse gate worktree;
  - [rejected] ends a round, [remote rejected] is unlanded remote, anything else goes to reconcile_push. An unknown outcome keeps the attempt finalizing; the same C is re-pushed while the tip is still B;
  - round limits; MOE_LAND_TARGET_CHECKED_OUT; peel/moe/work-<date> retired; MOE_PUSH_REBASE ignored.
- The unlanded route: rescue ref plus finalize_attempt 'unlanded'. The daemon sets landingRetry and routes REVIEW to WORKING (BLOCKED for diverged or a 3rd consecutive failure). The next pre-flight merges the target into W and prompts LANDING-CONFLICT:/LANDING-RETRY:. Replay settles a journaled C and never re-lands.
- The control-seat no-op (MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT).
- Board snapshots on refs/moe/board.
- moe/control: follow at L13, at the loop top before the hot-reload check and in the QA pre-flight with its ancestry check; MOE_WRAPPER_IN_WORKTREE.
- Removal at DONE by the QA post-flight (task_branch_landed) and the orphan sweep (interval, lock, 5 per pass, worktree-orphan rescue, links unlinked first). Moe touches only .worktrees/task-*.
- The migration is `--land-branch`, never a human merge (runbook: TROUBLESHOOTING, WT-16).
- Name the landed test files.

Error handling: describe each failure path's code and outcome as the code implements it; never paraphrase a refusal into a fallback. The test for this step is the step-6 greps.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, `## Delivery Path`: add a `### Worktree mode` subsection after the crash/replay paragraphs and before the 'five record directories' paragraph. Wrap at the file's ~80 columns; about 15-25 lines.
Content:
- `settings.worktreeMode` ('off' until the epic's final task). claim_next_task pins `workspaceMode` on the attempt and exposes `workspace: { mode, path, branch, target }`.
- A worker's bytes live in its task worktree on moe/task/<taskId>.
- The wrapper lands a completion as one squash commit on the target: `merge-tree` B T, the gate on that merged tree while a qualityGate is set, the journal, then publication. Local mode publishes with a CAS update-ref. Remote mode publishes with a non-forced push, which is the only publication; the local target is a mirror; an unknown push outcome keeps the attempt finalizing until a fetch settles it.
- A landing that cannot publish closes the attempt `unlanded`. The daemon routes the row back with `Task.landingRetry`, which is state only.
- Board history goes to refs/moe/board.
- The control checkout sits on moe/control and fast-forwards. QA reviews only landed commits.
- Shared mode is unchanged.
Keep the existing `**The daemon is state-only.**` invariant text untouched, and say explicitly that worktree mode adds daemon state (workspaceMode, landingRetry, the outcome) but no daemon git write.
Match WT-17's MCP_SERVER/SCHEMA spellings if those have landed.

Root CLAUDE.md, 'Working in this repo' and the package table.
(a) **Landing** bullet: append a compact worktree-mode summary.
- `settings.worktreeMode: 'on'` gives each WORKING claim its own `.worktrees/<taskId>` on `moe/task/<taskId>`. Checkpoints land there.
- A completion lands on the target (a literal `consolidationBranch`, else `main`) as one merge-tree squash commit published by CAS or a non-forced push after the gate. A conflict takes the unlanded route back to a worker.
- Board history goes to `refs/moe/board`; the control checkout sits on `moe/control` and fast-forwards. Point to scripts/CLAUDE.md for detail.
(b) `.moe/` bullet: one clause saying the BOARD staging described there is shared mode, and that worktree mode snapshots the board to refs/moe/board instead.
(c) Settings list: add `worktreeMode` and `consolidationBranch`.
(d) moe-vscode/ row: the VS Code note. Worktree mode needs no extension change: search honours .gitignore, which ignores .worktrees/ (§7.5).
(e) moe-jetbrains/ row: only if WT-15 landed without saying so, add that the plugin excludes <project>/.worktrees from the project model.
Keep sentences short; no other edits.

Worker role docs. Keep the 40-line cap: edit lines in place and add NO line to worker.md.

docs/roles/worker.md:
- Line 12 (qualityGate): add that in worktree mode the gate runs on EVERY completion, not just the epic-final one.
- Line 13: replace 'it commits FROM THE PROJECT ROOT, so work in the project root by default (never a `.worktrees/` checkout)' with mode-aware wording:
  - The wrapper lands from where it started you: the project root in shared mode, or your task worktree (`.worktrees/<taskId>`, branch `moe/task/<taskId>`) in worktree mode. Work there and run no git commands.
  - Any other `.worktrees/` checkout is human-directed only (see the using-git-worktrees row in worker.reference.md) and never landed. Per WT-S comment-ce2c4ee6, do not forbid those outright.
- Keep every daemon-test sentinel: 'what Moe supplied', 'truncated, omitted or missing', 'a navigation aid, never a reason to skip a read', 'once per session', 'isolated-clone delivery', 'moe.record_commit', 'fresh remote fetch', 'sessionId'. NO concrete task id: worker.md is in the stable system prefix, and targetedContextGuidance.test.ts fails on `task-<32 hex>`.

docs/roles/worker.reference.md:
- using-git-worktrees row: mode-aware.
- 'Commits, checkpoints and rescue refs' table: give each Where cell its worktree-mode destination (completion on the target as one squash commit; wip on moe/task/<taskId>). Add a row: a worktree completion that cannot reach the target lands nothing on it; rescue ref, and the task returns to WORKING with landingRetry.
- Attribution paragraph: in worktree mode there are no tiers. Every non-DENY path in your worktree lands; DENY still holds (.moe/** with no BOARD exception, .claude/skills/**); edits outside the worktree are reported as MOE_WORKTREE_STRAY_EDIT and never landed.
- Practical rules: mark the 'shared checkout is dirty' rule as shared mode. Add a LANDING-CONFLICT:/LANDING-RETRY: bullet per §2.5: the wrapper already merged the target into your worktree; edit files only (no git commands, no new plan), remove every conflict marker, re-run the plan's verification command, then complete_task.
- Keep the reference sentinels 'memory-name inventory' and 'once per session'.

Regenerate the vendored role docs. Precedent: 47b4e438 shipped initFiles.ts with its role-doc edit. The daemon writes ROLE_DOCS into every project's .moe/roles/, and targetedContextGuidance/qaCommitPolicy tests check both copies.
- The generator (packages/moe-daemon/scripts/generate-init-files.ts) reads git history for the shipped-body sha list. So run it in a `git clone -q --shared /mnt/d/projexts/moes <tmp>` with the two edited worker docs copied in: `cd <tmp>/packages/moe-daemon && npm ci && npm run generate-init-files`.
- Copy ONLY src/generated/initFiles.ts back.
- NEVER run npm ci/build/clean in the shared checkout: its node_modules are Windows builds and a live daemon may use its dist. Never touch packages/moe-proxy.
- Check `git diff -- packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts`: it must change only the worker.md / worker.reference.md entries and their markers or sha lists. Any other doc's hunk means HEAD's copy was stale. Report it in the completion summary; do not hand-edit it out.
Error handling: if the clone, npm ci or the generator fails, stop and report_blocked with the error. Never commit a hand-edited initFiles.ts.

Verification: run ONCE, fresh, from the repo root, as ONE command: `<checkRefs[0]> && <checkRefs[1]>`, both exactly as in the executionContract.
- checkRefs[0]: npm run lint, plus greps that fail on today's docs. It also compares the `- **Land on every exit**` line with HEAD's to prove the shared-mode bullet is untouched; run it BEFORE the landing commit.
- checkRefs[1]: copies the six files into a `git clone --shared` of HEAD and runs parity-check on HEAD's scripts (WT-S comment-2f5b6786). It then runs `npm ci && npm run build` in the clone's packages/moe-daemon, `cmp`s the regenerated initFiles.ts with yours, and runs the targetedContextGuidance, qaCommitPolicy and initFiles vitest files.
Expected: exit 0. Submit the joined command, its exit code and the tail to complete_task.

Adversarial self-review: one pass over the whole diff before complete_task.
(a) Accuracy: every helper, code, env var, ref and setting named in the five docs exists with that spelling in the landed wrappers or daemon. No design-only name is presented as shipped; grep each one.
(b) No contradiction with WT-17's MCP_SERVER/SCHEMA/CONFIGURATION text or WT-16's TROUBLESHOOTING runbook, if landed.
(c) Safety wording keeps its negatives intact: never forced, never a local CAS fallback in remote mode, never auto-resolved, never re-landed by replay, never deletes an unlanded commit without a rescue ref, the daemon never writes git.
(d) Shared-mode text unchanged everywhere it is not explicitly marked as shared mode; worker.md still ≤40 lines.
(e) worker.md carries no concrete task id and keeps every sentinel.
(f) initFiles.ts changed only for the worker docs.
Fix anything found, rerun the step-6 command, then complete_task.

Spike self-review note (docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §1.1, §2.2 L8/L9, §2.6, §6.2). For the worktree arm of "Land on every exit" in scripts/CLAUDE.md, and for ARCHITECTURE.md:

Planner note from architect-4ff0711c. Task-31187ec1 (plan rev 1) adds a worker pre-flight refusal code, MOE_WORKTREE_CONTEXT_FAILED, in both wrappers. planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Editing the 6.4k-char shared-mode Land bullet in place: rejected. DoD 2 requires it unchanged, and a separate bullet keeps the diff reviewable.
- Skipping initFiles.ts: rejected. The daemon would keep writing the old worker docs into projects, and precedent 47b4e438 ships both.
- Regenerating from a git-archive snapshot: rejected, because the generator needs git history; a `git clone --shared` has it without touching the shared checkout.
- The task's original verification greps: 'worktree' already matches scripts/CLAUDE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md today, so they are strengthened to strings that fail before the edit.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Role docs reach agents two ways: the plugin bundle and the daemon's vendored ROLE_DOCS (initFiles.ts), which writes and upgrades .moe/roles/ by marker sha. Daemon tests guard sentinel phrases in both the source and the generated copies. worker.md sits in the launchers' stable system prefix, so it must hold no per-task content. WT-17 owns MCP_SERVER/SCHEMA/CONFIGURATION, WT-16 owns TROUBLESHOOTING, and WT-19 re-checks all docs and receives mismatch reports.
planningNotes.risks:
- Design-only spellings: the doc predates the code and planners changed details (e.g. WT-09/WT-10M/WT-11), so verify every name against landed code.
- A summary that drops a 'never' qualifier would teach agents an unsafe fallback.
- The npm ci in the clone needs the npm cache or network.
- HEAD's initFiles.ts may already be stale for another doc: report it, don't hide it.
- Running the Land-bullet HEAD comparison after the landing commit is vacuous; run it before.
- Never run npm ci/build/clean in the shared checkout's packages (Windows node_modules, live dist).
